Both Ms Hanson and Mr Taylor addressed CPAC — a spin-off of conservative conferences held in the US and UK — on Saturday morning, taking aim at the Albanese government and pitching themselves as the conservative alternative.
It was the first time a Coalition leader has addressed the annual forum, although notable Liberal figures like Tony Abbott and Jacinta Nampijinpa Price have addressed it in recent years.
But while Senator Hanson sharply criticised the Coalition, Mr Taylor made almost no mention of One Nation.
His speech made just one apparent indirect reference to Senator Hanson, referencing her dominance of the One Nation party and brand.
"Good government isn't built around one figure. You need a strong team," he said.
And he opened the speech by referencing a number of "mistakes" the Coalition made in government, acknowledging to the audience that "some of you may have doubts".
He pointed to areas like immigration policy, climate change and government spending during the pandemic as policy failures under Coalition governments.
"We made the mistake as a government of signing up to net zero," he said.
"Your frustrations about where we let you down in the recent past are understandable and reasonable. Believe me, I share them."
Both leaders reserved their strongest attacks for the Albanese government — Mr Taylor arguing it was leaving Australians "poorer, weaker, and demoralised", and Senator Hanson calling it "wretched and corrupt".
Hanson says ON would work with Coalition
Despite her strong rhetoric on the Coalition, Senator Hanson made clear that One Nation would work with them if it meant changing the government.
"One Nation will work with the Liberals and Nationals to remove this horrible Labor government and deliver something better," she said.
"That's what you, the people, want. It's the will of the people."
In a later press conference, she clarified that the offer extended to supply and confidence only — not a formal coalition.
"We will give them the numbers if they need it to form government, but I hope it's going to be the other way around," she said.
"So if we have the numbers, they will give us the numbers to form government. I don't want seats around their [cabinet] table."
She referenced her time in prison after a 2003 conviction for electoral fraud, later quashed on appeal, under the Howard government, but said she would put "personal grievances aside".
"Yes, I do have reasons to hold a grudge, but I also have children and grandchildren," she said.
"Their futures and your futures matter more."
In a later speech, Nationals leader Matt Canavan also struck a more conciliatory tone, urging those on the right of politics not to become caught up fighting among themselves.
"My message to you today is, look, we do wear lots of different colours. I get that," he said.
"There's lots of different people here.
"But the one thing we have to do at the next election is all put the Labor Party last. That's what we've got to do."

Ukraine, US and European talks in Miami end early
Talks between representatives of the United States, Ukraine, European countries and NATO in Miami on ways to de-escalate and end the war have ended earlier than planned.
Source: Alex Raufoglu, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty's senior Washington correspondent; the US President's Special Envoy Steve Witkoff
Quote from Raufoglu: "Miami talks concluded sooner than planned. 'No second day,' sources tell me."
Details: Witkoff said that participants in the meeting had "held constructive discussions on potential avenues to de-escalate and conclude the war with Russia ahead of winter and advance efforts toward a durable and lasting peace".
"The discussions covered a broad range of issues, including near-term measures related to winter preparedness (energy resilience, grains exports), security guarantees, as well as longer-term arrangements for Ukraine's and Europe's security to prevent future conflicts, and support Ukraine's post-war reconstruction and economic prosperity, including EU accession," he wrote.
Witkoff stressed that the productive exchange of views had helped identify areas of work ahead of the United States' next contacts with Russia.
Background:
- On 8 October, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that talks would take place in the US involving a Ukrainian delegation. This delegation included Davyd Arakhamiia, leader of the Servant of the People party; Rustem Umierov, Head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service; Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine; and Serhii Kyslytsia, First Deputy Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine.
- Ahead of the meeting, Axios reported, citing US and Ukrainian officials, that US President's Special Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were planning to present "new ideas and proposals" in Miami to break the diplomatic deadlock.
- On 9 October, US President Donald Trump said he had had a "highly successful discussion" with Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin and reached an agreement on lifting sanctions on Russian diesel fuel.
- Zelenskyy strongly criticised Trump's actions, describing the easing of sanctions as an "absolutely terrible" move. He stressed that this "happy birthday present for Putin" will provide Russia with billions more to continue the war
- Zelenskyy said Ukraine's negotiating team in the US was being used as "cover" while Trump and Putin reached agreements on fuel supplies.
- Yuri Ushakov, an aide to Vladimir Putin, said that the Russian leader had rejected the prospect of peace talks and stressed that Russia will continue fighting until it has achieved "all its objectives" during a phone call with US President Donald Trump.

Suvendu eyes Bengal sweep: Can TMC, Congress unite to challenge BJP?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-10
15:44:18 UTC
00:44:18 KST

"We are set to win 42 out of 42 in the 2029 Lok Sabha election." West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari had made this grandiose claim even before the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll results. A visibly buoyant Adhikari reiterated the target after his party swept both seats. Victories in both constituencies were expected, yet the margins, particularly in Rejinagar, where roughly 70% of voters are Muslim, came as a revelation. With the all-important Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls likely to be held in late November, there is a perception that the BJP may win handsomely. It is up to the Opposition to put up a spirited fight.
Bypolls have usually favoured the ruling party
What may give the Opposition some solace is the fact that bypolls, at least over the last decade or so, have followed an extremely predictable pattern in Bengal. Between the 2021 and 2026 Assembly elections, Trinamool won 20 of the 21 Assembly bypolls held in the state. Its dominance was particularly striking in 2024, when it swept all 12 by-elections, including four seats previously held by BJP legislators.In July 2024, Trinamool wrested Raiganj, Ranaghat Dakshin and Bagdah from the BJP despite the latter's electoral strength in these areas during the Lok Sabha election just weeks earlier.
In November, TMC captured Madarihat, which the BJP had held since 2016. Even in June 2025, less than a year before its Assembly rout, Trinamool retained Kaliganj by more than 50,000 votes.
Suvendu's promise
There have been exceptions to the incumbent's advantage. In 2023, Congress, supported by the Left, defeated the ruling TMC in Sagardighi by nearly 23,000 votes. However, the MLA concerned, Bayron Biswas, soon joined TMC.
Why BJP's victories still matter
In Nandigram, BJP's Hasi Rani Rath defeated Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, who had Mamata's support, by 1,22,753 votes. In Rejinagar, BJP's Shankharavh Sarkar defeated Aam Janata Unnayan Party candidate Golam Nabi Azad, son of party founder Humayun Kabir, by more than 75,000 votes.In both constituencies, BJP polled more votes than all its opponents combined. Rejinagar witnessed notable outreach from the CM, with Suvendu even saying that Muslims did not need to chant "Jai Shri Ram". He also urged them to turn over a new leaf and extend a hand of friendship to the new government.Following the result, Adhikari attributed BJP's success partly to support from beneficiaries of the Annapurna welfare scheme, under which eligible women receive ₹3,000 per month. Whether the BJP can really secure a share of the Muslim vote in elections with bigger stakes remains to be seen. But if it does, Suvendu's dream of a clean sweep in the Lok Sabha election may well look more realistic.
Allegations of electoral excesses
The Opposition, though, has refused to grant legitimacy to the Assembly bypolls, citing alleged malpractices by the ruling machinery. Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar demanded fresh elections in both constituencies, alleging booth capturing, intimidation, bogus voting and the forcible removal of polling agents. AJUP, which had won the seat previously, alleged that its candidate received zero votes in 33 booths and just one vote in another 19 booths. Mamata's TMC faction made similar allegations of rigging, while the rival Trinamool faction and the Left also complained about polling agents being prevented from functioning.In Nandigram, Congress candidate Milan Pradhan alleged that party agents had been driven out of booths and voters prevented from voting. His earlier arrest in connection with an old case related to the Nandigram land movement had already prompted allegations of political harassment.
BJP supporters in Rejinagar
BJP rejected the rigging allegations, maintaining that polling was peaceful. The Election Commission described voting as largely peaceful despite receiving complaints. One widely circulated claim that BJP had received more votes than the number of registered voters at a Rejinagar booth was subsequently rebutted by election officials, who said the original electorate figure was incorrect.Such allegations are not new to Bengal's electoral politics, one of the reasons why the opposition have frequently asked for central forces to conduct polls. The 2018 panchayat elections witnessed widespread reports of violence and intimidation. More than a third of the seats were won uncontested, overwhelmingly by Trinamool, amid allegations that opposition candidates had been prevented from filing nominations. A year later, the BJP increased its Lok Sabha tally in Bengal from two seats in 2014 to 18 in 2019.Political observers have linked that breakthrough partly to resentment over the conduct of the panchayat polls. Very recently, Abhishek Banerjee’s Diamond Harbour model of winning by record margin of votes had also come under scrutiny. For BJP though, barely a few months into power, the chances of pushback to any alleged excesses remain relatively modest.
What's next for the Opposition?
The INDIA bloc has upped the ante in the capital, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote manipulation during the SIR process. Leaders such as Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee and even those from the Left have been sharing the stage. With a common goal, the confluence is organic. But the state-level dynamics are very different, something that has affected the INDIA alliance for a long time.An INDIA alliance is unlikely to become a reality in Bengal, with Left and TMC cadres rarely seeing eye to eye. An alliance between Mamata's TMC and Congress remains an open question, with state leaders of the grand old party lukewarm about giving space to a leader who did not allow them much room to grow while in power.Mamata came to power in 2011 in alliance with Congress, but the two soon parted ways. Since then, the parties have hardly worked together politically, until this by-election. There have been several overtures from Congress in the past, but these were rebuffed by the then West Bengal CM, who wanted to maximise her political capital. Now that the script has flipped, Congress may not give in so easily.Former state Congress president Pradip Bhattacharya disclosed in September that the state leadership had advised against a proposed bypoll arrangement under which Congress would contest Nandigram and Mamata's Trinamool would fight Rejinagar. Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury's recent invitation to Mamata to return to Congress with her remaining MLAs and MPs came with a condition about leaving behind her political baggage, widely interpreted as a reference to Abhishek Banerjee.Even the Nandigram understanding was not a formal seat-sharing arrangement. Mamata supported Milan Pradhan after her faction's candidate withdrew. In Rejinagar, both parties contested separately. Many Congress leaders believe that it is time to rebuild the party in the state when opposition space is up for grabs. The BJP is still getting to grips with governance, and teething troubles in several areas, including the rollout of government schemes, have made headlines.The organisational crisis within Trinamool adds another dimension. Following the Assembly defeat, the party split into rival factions, prompting the Election Commission to temporarily freeze its original name and symbol. The Mamata-led faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee-led Democratic Trinamool Congress contested under different identities in the bypolls. Neither performed well. In Rejinagar, Mamata's faction received 3,847 votes, while Democratic Trinamool polled 2,044.
Mamata Banerjee's political journey before becoming CM
The Left, meanwhile, continues to face the challenge of translating political visibility into electoral support. Younger leaders such as Satarup Ghosh, Dipshita Dhar and Srijan Bhattacharya have attracted attention, particularly on social media, but the party's electoral recovery remains limited.There were, however, modest improvements in the latest bypolls. In Nandigram, the CPI's Santi Gopal Giri increased his tally from 2,997 votes in May to 5,779. Congress also improved its vote count in both constituencies, although the Nandigram comparison is complicated by Mamata's support for its candidate.
Municipal elections: The next big battle
The immediate electoral focus now shifts to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal polls, where voting is tentatively expected in late November. The stakes extend far beyond the two Assembly bypolls.In the 2021 Kolkata Municipal Corporation election, Trinamool won 134 of 144 wards, securing more than 72% of the votes. BJP won just three wards and Congress two. Interestingly, the Left Front, with nearly 12% of the vote, finished ahead of BJP in vote share despite winning fewer seatstThe forthcoming election will also be fought on a substantially altered map. Kolkata's wards have increased from 144 to 209, and Howrah's from 50 to 68. For both factions of TMC, this election will be the first major test of who enjoys greater public support. For Mamata Banerjee, south Kolkata remains her pocket borough, and following the humiliating defeat in Bhabanipur, she would be desperate to turn around her fortunes. For Firhad Hakim and others, it will be an opportunity to prove that they can win on their own without Didi's support.Congress and the Left have long been marginal forces in both Kolkata and Howrah, barring a few pockets. The Left appears inclined to contest independently in several areas, although the CPM has encouraged local discussions with Congress. Some Congress district leaders, meanwhile, have argued that the party should contest all 209 Kolkata wards on its own.The decisions are yet to be finalised, leaving Congress with a difficult choice between rebuilding independently, cooperating with the Left and exploring an understanding with Mamata.
Road to 2029
Nationally, Rahul Gandhi's success in rallying different INDIA bloc parties in the campaign demanding the resignation of the CEC has done his popularity no harm. The bonhomie between Sonia Gandhi and Mamata Banerjee at the recent press conference was there for everyone to see. They have maintained cordial personal relations despite the ebbs and flows in their political exchanges. But the political calculations in Bengal remain very different. Rahul's pointed attacks on Trinamool over corruption during the Assembly campaign had reinforced the Congress's adversarial position in the state. For local Congress workers, a sudden statewide alliance with Mamata would require a significant political adjustment. Didi however, remains in the frontlines in the protest against Election Commission and was detained on Saturday even as Rahul Gandhi skipped the protest and went to Chennai.
Former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee detained during protest in New Delhi
At the same time, Mamata faces one of the most difficult phases of her political career, while the BJP confronts increasingly coordinated opposition protests at the national level. Hence the political equations could well change. After the municipal elections in Kolkata and Howrah, polls in more than 100 other civic bodies are expected next year, followed by panchayat polls in 2028 and the Lok Sabha election in 2029. Those who have power in the grassroots are likely to have a headstart in the Lok Sabha election.Suvendu has already set his sights on winning all 42 Lok Sabha seats in Bengal. Such a result would have significant implications for the BJP's national parliamentary tally. For Congress, the calculation is therefore not confined to the revival of its Bengal organisation. Its leadership must also consider the wider political ramifications of allowing the BJP a free-run in the state.
For the Opposition, national unity over electoral issues is one thing. Building an effective political arrangement in Bengal is quite another. The coming municipal elections will provide the first major opportunity to see whether those differences can be bridged.

Chile declares part of Santiago disaster zone after heavy rains
Floods in Las Contes, affluent suburb of capital Santiago, leave 6 people injured, force evacuations, sweep vehicles through streets
Maryam Ashalem de Andres
10 October 2026•Update: 10 October 2026
ISTANBUL
Chile on Friday declared part of the capital Santiago a disaster zone after torrential rains triggered flash floods and mudslides, leaving at least six people injured and forcing evacuations, according to local media reports.
The declaration for Las Condes, an affluent suburb of the capital, allows public agencies to adopt extraordinary measures to coordinate emergency assistance, assess damage, and support recovery efforts.
Heavy rain on Thursday sent torrents of water and mud through streets, swept away vehicles, and inundated homes.
The Mapocho River also overflowed, while flooding made roads impassable and prompted emergency crews to respond to calls for help.
Las Condes Mayor Catalina San Martin said 14.4 centimeters (5.7 inches) of rain had fallen in recent days, around nine times the average October rainfall, leaving the ground saturated and raising the risk of additional flooding and landslides.
At least six people were reportedly injured, including a one-year-old who suffered fractures.
Firefighters rescued or evacuated more than 1,000 people as emergency teams worked to assist residents, clear debris, and restore access to affected areas.
The National Disaster Prevention and Response Service also declared a red alert for 10 municipalities in mountainous and foothill areas of the Santiago Metropolitan Region due to the risk of additional landslides.
Authorities urged residents to follow official safety instructions as emergency services continued to assess the damage and respond to potential new incidents.
The flooding affected homes and infrastructure in the area, with emergency crews working to remove mud and debris from streets and help residents whose properties were damaged.
The disaster comes during spring in the Southern Hemisphere, when intense rainfall can trigger flash floods and landslides, particularly in areas where the ground has become saturated.
The government said the disaster zone declaration would help coordinate public services and provide assistance to affected households as recovery efforts continue.

Under new regulations, Türkiye bans children under 15 from social media
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-10
02:51:25 UTC
11:51:25 KST

Merve Aydogan
10 October 2026•Update: 10 October 2026
Türkiye has barred social network providers from offering services to minors under the age of 15, according to new Cyber Security Directorate regulations published Saturday in the Official Gazette.
The regulation said providers "cannot provide services to children who have not reached the age of 15."
Providers must also offer differentiated services and take necessary measures for users 15 and older, according to the regulations, adding that they should consider the minor’s best interests and their physical, mental, psychological, social, and emotional development.
Age verification must prioritize personal data protection, using methods that determine only whether a user meets the age threshold rather than establishing identity, it added.
Saying that providers must make the reliability of verification methods, their algorithm structures, and child-focused service policies "clear, auditable and testable for users, parents and the directorate," it stressed that they must create clear, user-friendly parental control tools.
The regulations come under new legislation on social media passed by the Turkish parliament this April.

Asia-Pacific Community: China's Yunnan-grown coffee gains ground on New Zealand cafe menus
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-10
10:33:51 CST
11:33:51 KST

WELLINGTON, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- Cafes across New Zealand's major cities are pouring more cups brewed with coffee beans from China's Yunnan Province, whose diverse, distinctive flavor profiles are winning over local coffee lovers.
Coffee drinkers in New Zealand have long associated quality coffee with well-established growing powerhouses: Brazil, Colombia and Ethiopia. But a new origin is making inroads on the global coffee circuit -- China's Yunnan.
MQ Coffee, headquartered in Auckland, New Zealand's largest city, is among the businesses helping Yunnan coffee gain a foothold in New Zealand. Wang Yanqi, co-founder of MQ Coffee, said that the quality of Yunnan coffee has improved significantly in recent years, and overseas consumers are paying increasing attention to China as a coffee-producing origin.
MQ Coffee currently carries out coffee product customization, production and packaging of drip coffee bags, and coffee training in New Zealand, while introducing Yunnan coffee to local consumers and coffee professionals through cupping sessions, professional training and origin exchanges.
"Personally, I think Yunnan specialty beans are getting better and better year by year," said Zhang Xue, a coffee taster and coffee trainer in New Zealand, adding that Yunnan specialty coffee is becoming increasingly attractive in terms of flavor expression and quality consistency.
Yunnan has formed six core coffee-producing regions: Pu'er, Baoshan, Lincang, Dehong, Xishuangbanna and Nujiang. Pu'er coffee and Baoshan small-bean coffee have been included on the mutual recognition and protection list under the agreement on China-EU geographical indications.
According to Kunming Customs statistics, in the first eight months of 2026, Yunnan exported 11,000 tonnes of coffee worth 450 million yuan (about 67 million U.S. dollars), mainly to 42 countries and regions including Vietnam, Malaysia and Germany, ranking first nationwide by export value. In 2025, Yunnan exported 195.6 tonnes of green coffee beans to New Zealand, worth 10.2 million yuan.
Some Yunnan coffees deliver good sweetness and body and retain distinct coffee flavors with milk added, making them well-suited to milk-based coffee drinks familiar to New Zealand consumers. Meanwhile, finely processed Yunnan coffees can develop richer layers of floral and fruity aromas via pour-over and drip brewing, Wang noted.
New Zealand's coffee market is operating with a relatively mature industry chain covering importation, roasting, wholesale and retail. For Chinese coffee products that have just entered the local market, building stable sales channels, expanding consumer groups, and turning consumers' initial novelty into lasting competitiveness remain key challenges to address, according to local coffee market observers.
To raise recognition of Yunnan coffee, MQ Coffee has organized New Zealand coffee professionals and enthusiasts to visit Yunnan's growing regions to learn about local coffee farming and processing practices.
For repeat purchases from foreign consumers, Yunnan coffee must further boost its competitiveness in product quality, pricing and supply stability, Wang said. ■

Red Cross to fund evacuation of around 90 rural households from Donetsk region
The Donetsk Regional Military Administration’s Department of Agricultural Development and Land Relations told an Ukrinform correspondent.
“About 90 households in the Donetsk region have so far submitted applications and the required documents to receive financial assistance from the International Committee of the Red Cross to evacuate livestock, poultry and equipment. The detention of agricultural workers in the Donetsk region was linked to their inability to find transportation to evacuate their animals, and this problem is now being addressed,” the Department of Agricultural Development and Land Relations of the Donetsk Regional Military Administration said.
As reported, the ICRC financial assistance program is aimed at supporting economically vulnerable households in evacuating livestock, essential agricultural equipment and means of livelihood from communities where mandatory or partial evacuation has been announced.
The project has been launched in the Kramatorsk district of the Donetsk region, as well as in the Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk regions. The amount of financial assistance is UAH 65,000 per household.

Mexico convicts 3 in murders of Australian, US surfers
October 10, 2026
A Mexican court on Friday convicted three men in the 2024 murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend, who were killed during a botched robbery which sparked international outrage.
Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, aged 30 and 33, and their friend Carter Rhoad, 30, were on a surfing trip to Mexico when they were shot dead in Baja California state.
They were camping in a remote beachside area near the city of Ensenada when they were attacked during a suspected robbery. Their bodies were found days later, in a well, with gunshot wounds to their heads.
What was said in court?
The judge on Friday ruled that the three Mexican defendants had acted with premeditation. They are yet to be sentenced for the murders.
The prosecution has asked for an "exemplary sentence" of 210 years for each of the three convicted, even though the maximum sentence in Baja California is 60 years.
Debra Robinson, mother to the Australian brothers, burst into tears when the court passed the guilty verdict.
"While no verdict can ever bring back our boys or ease the heartbreak of losing them," the convictions marked "an important step towards justice and accountability," their father Martin Robinson said in a statement on behalf of the family.
Victim begged for mercy
Case prosecutors described the killings of the three surfers during the closing arguments on Thursday, by recalling the testimony of the girlfriend of one of the main suspects.
She had said that Rhoad had begged for his life while her boyfriend had bragged about "how beautifully" his victims cried before he robbed them.
The triple homicide shocked Mexico and drew international attention when it came to light.
Baja California is one of Mexico's most violent states, riddled with organized crime and drug trafficking, although cartel activity doesn't usually affect tourists.

First hurricane to hit US in two years: Isaias slams Florida with 105 mph winds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-10
02:17:12 UTC
11:17:12 KST

Hurricane Isaias struck the U.S. Gulf Coast on Friday night, becoming the first hurricane to make landfall in the United States in two years, as residents who had not evacuated rushed to complete their preparations against destructive winds, dangerous storm surge and torrential rain.
The storm made landfall near Destin in the Florida Panhandle, close to the Alabama border, with sustained winds of around 105 mph (170 kph), according to the National Hurricane Center.
Isaias had earlier intensified into a Category 3 hurricane but weakened to Category 2 before reaching shore. Despite the weakening, forecasters warned that it remained capable of causing extensive damage and life-threatening flooding.
Rain began falling along parts of the Gulf Coast on Friday morning, and tropical storm conditions spread across the region as the hurricane approached.
The National Hurricane Center warned that Category 3 hurricanes, classified as major hurricanes, can cause devastating damage. Although Isaias weakened before landfall, its powerful winds and heavy rainfall remained serious threats.
The storm was expected to weaken rapidly as it moved inland, potentially becoming a tropical storm by Saturday afternoon while tracking northward through Alabama toward the Mississippi border.
"Preparations should be completed quickly, as weather conditions will deteriorate rapidly," the hurricane center warned in an advisory issued early Friday.
"Although the storm is not expected to make landfall at peak intensity, Isaias will likely still be a major hurricane when it reaches the coast," the earlier advisory said.
Dangerous storm surge, flooding and tornadoes
Beyond the powerful winds, forecasters warned of a dangerous storm surge reaching 6 to 9 feet (1.8 to 2.7 meters) in some coastal areas, along with heavy rainfall and the possibility of tornadoes.
Rainfall totals of 4 to 8 inches (100 to 200 millimeters) were expected across parts of the region during the weekend, with isolated areas potentially receiving as much as 15 inches (380 millimeters).
Such rainfall could trigger flash flooding, particularly in low-lying communities and areas already saturated by earlier rain.
Isaias is the first hurricane to strike the U.S. coastline since Hurricane Milton hit Florida on October 9, 2024, exactly two years earlier.
As the storm approached, residents were seen boarding up windows, filling sandbags and securing their homes.
Thousands of National Guard troops were deployed to assist with preparations and emergency response operations.
Several counties issued mandatory evacuation orders for vulnerable coastal communities, while videos shared on social media showed heavy traffic on roads leading away from the threatened areas.
Double red flags were raised on beaches, warning of extremely dangerous water conditions.
The governors of Florida and Alabama declared states of emergency across dozens of counties, allowing authorities to mobilize additional resources ahead of the storm.
On Dauphin Island, a barrier island off the Alabama coast, authorities encouraged residents to evacuate voluntarily.
Mayor Jeff Collier said he did not expect extensive damage but emphasized that hurricanes can change course or intensify unexpectedly.
"These things are very fickle, and a little jog here or there, or some last-minute increase in strength, we just have to be prepared for the worst," he said.
An unusually quiet hurricane season
Isaias is the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, which has been unusually quiet.
For the first time in 75 years, no Atlantic hurricane had formed by the end of September, making this one of the latest starts to hurricane activity in decades.
The storm is the ninth named system of the Atlantic season, but the previous eight never developed beyond tropical storm strength.
Most of those storms formed between mid-August and September.
The latest seasonal forecast had projected between seven and 13 named storms, with two to six potentially strengthening into hurricanes.
In an average Atlantic hurricane season, approximately 14 named storms form, including seven hurricanes.
The Atlantic hurricane season officially runs from June 1 through November 30.
Although Isaias was expected to lose strength as it moved inland, forecasters warned that heavy rainfall, flooding and damaging winds could continue affecting communities well beyond the immediate coastline.
For residents who remained in the storm's path, authorities emphasized that the danger would not end once the hurricane's center moved away.

Ukraine attacks Russia with spy balloons

Ukraine attacks Russia with spy balloons
Ukrainian spy balloons have been spotted over central Russia’s Yaroslavl Region for the first time, according to the regional Security Ministry.
Local authorities said several of the small flying objects were successfully shot down on Friday, urging residents to report anything suspicious that they see in the sky or suspected debris to emergency services.
The balloons “had been launched from the territory of Ukraine,” according to officials. Small reconnaissance balloons can be used to distract enemy air defenses, but they can also serve as reconnaissance platforms, including to pinpoint the locations of air defense systems or help direct strikes against other targets.
Yaroslavl Region has been targeted by Ukrainian long-range strikes in recent weeks. In mid-September, the Russian military shot down 65 drones over the region in a single day during a large-scale drone raid targeting a local refinery.
Although Friday’s incident was the first of its kind reported in Yaroslavl Region, the Russian military has encountered Ukrainian spy balloons and even explosive-laden balloons in the past.
In September 2025, the Ukrainian military attempted to strike several Russian regions with dozens of meteorological balloons carrying explosives.
The Wall Street Journal claimed in a February article that Kiev had been using high-altitude balloons in attacks on Russia since the Ukraine conflict escalated in 2022. However, according to the Russian Defense Ministry, such attacks were first detected in autumn 2024, with another surge in reported incidents in late summer 2025.
The recent balloon attacks come as Russia has stepped up strikes on missile and drone warehouses, as well as unmanned aerial vehicle assembly facilities, in response to continued Ukrainian strikes on Russian civilian and energy infrastructure, which Moscow describes as terrorist acts.
After Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky recently threatened to step up attacks on Russian oil refineries, Moscow vowed to intensify strikes on Ukraine’s military-related facilities while maintaining that it never targets civilians.
On Wednesday, the Russian military targeted a Smart Ammunition facility used to assemble and store FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles, FP-9 tactical ballistic missiles, and components for both weapons, as well as other sites across several Ukrainian regions, including a drone workshop in Kirovograd Region and the JTI Ukraine tobacco factory in Kremenchug, which Russian officials say is used to manufacture small-arms ammunition.

solid walnut, oak, and padauk give bathroom flush plates a sculptural identity
RTY studio introduces solid wood flush plates combining precise geometry with the warmth and individual grain of american walnut, european oak and padauk.
Solid wood gives a functional bathroom detail a sculptural form
RTY Studio has developed a collection of solid wood flush plates for Geberit Sigma systems, combining precise geometry with the grain and color variations of American walnut, European oak, and padauk. Designed and crafted in Zagreb, Croatia, by sculptor Tomislav Martinčević, a member of the Croatian Association of Artists (HDLU), the collection reinterprets a functional bathroom detail through material and form.
The three models feature clean geometric profiles, crisp upper corners, and rounded lower corners, with two flush buttons integrated into each wooden face. The natural grain and varying tones of the three wood species give each plate a distinct appearance.
CNC machining and hand finishing refine solid wood flush plates
Production combines CNC machining with hand sanding, edge refinement, and finishing to achieve precise dimensions and smooth transitions between surfaces. A protective finish provides water resistance while retaining the wood’s natural appearance and matte texture. Each plate combines a solid wood face with a magnetic mounting mechanism and stainless steel screws, concealing the installation hardware.
Alongside the standard collection, RTY Studio produces custom designs featuring geometric patterns, carved surfaces, and wood inlays. These variations extend the flush plate into a personalized design element that responds to the character of an interior.

Unknown Publisher

Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert AI servers with Nvidia chips to China
A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, a federal court filing showed on Oct 9.
Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun pleaded guilty to four counts, including conspiracies to violate US export controls, smuggle goods from the US, defraud the country and obstruct justice. He entered the plea on Oct 9 in the US District Court in Manhattan.
The United States and China are competing for dominance in artificial intelligence, with both investing billions of dollars in a technology seen as critical to economic growth, national security and military and cybersecurity capabilities.
In March, US prosecutors charged Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder of the AI-server maker, with conspiring to divert about US$2.5 billion worth of American AI technology to China in violation of export laws.
The scheme began around October 2023, with Sun and others conspiring to export servers from a US manufacturer, widely believed to be Super Micro, to China without the required licences, according to the indictment.
Asked for comment on the guilty plea, California-based Super Micro referred to its prior statements that the company was not named as a defendant in the indictment and that it had no impact on its business operations. 
Super Micro terminated Sun and cut ties with the other defendants earlier this year.
A lawyer for Sun declined to comment.
Also indicted were the co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang, who was a sales manager at Super Micro’s Taiwan office, while Sun was a contractor.
A lawyer for Liaw - who co-founded Super Micro in 1993 and joined its board in 2023 - did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Chang’s lawyer could not immediately be reached for comment.
The indictment described Sun as a broker and “fixer” who facilitated orders and took steps to conceal the scheme. 
He helped stage “dummy” servers in December 2025 and made false statements to a US Department of Commerce officer during an inspection of supposedly stored servers, which had already been diverted to China, according to the indictment.
Washington has restricted sales of advanced AI chips to China, citing national security concerns. The indictment said Nvidia’s B200, H100 and H200 graphics processing units, and servers containing them, were subject to the restrictions. REUTERS

Trump's diesel agreement with Putin accused of contradicting Russia sanctions law
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-10
02:09:00 UTC
11:09:00 KST

President Donald Trump's Friday announcement that Russia will supply diesel fuel to the global market marked an apparent pivot from recent efforts to pressure Moscow to end the Ukraine war by targeting Russian energy exports.
Trump claimed the move, unveiled with less than a month left in an affordability-focused midterm election, would swiftly bring down record-high diesel prices.
But commentators and critics were quick to highlight contradictions between the new policy and prior efforts by the U.S. to clamp down on Russian oil sales.
Those efforts most recently included the enactment of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, empowering Trump to impose tariffs up to 100% on the top purchasers of Russian crude oil or gas, among other restrictions. Trump signed the bill into law just three weeks ago.
"Congress just passed a law giving Trump the power to impose new tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil & gas," Scott Lincicome, vice president of the libertarian Cato Institute, said on X after Trump's Friday announcement.
"Can America tariff America?" he quipped.
Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., a member of the Senate Ukraine Caucus, accused Trump's latest move of being "directly contrary to Congress's intent in our bipartisan sanctions bill."
Peter Harrell, visiting scholar at Georgetown University Law Center's Institute of International Economic Law, in an X post said that the relaxation of Russian diesel restrictions "pretty much proves the point that the Graham Russia Bill was not going to force the Trump Administration to increase economic pressure on Moscow."
Some of the criticism crossed party lines.
"Through the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, we gave the president significant authorities and leverage against China and Russia to bring Putin's war to an end with a negotiated settlement," Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, said in an X post. "Unfortunately, while I understand the desire to bring down diesel prices, I am concerned the lifting of sanctions on Russian oil will only fund the Kremlin's war machine—emboldening more violence and destruction, as we have seen in recent days," McCaul said.
The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's questions about the diesel agreement with Russia.
Less than a year earlier, the Trump administration slapped sanctions on multiple Russian oil companies in response to what it called "Russia's lack of serious commitment to a peace process to end the war in Ukraine."
Trump also had previously slammed NATO allies for continuing to buy Russian oil. In a September 2025 Truth Social post, he wrote, "the purchase of Russian Oil, by some, has been shocking! It greatly weakens your negotiating position, and bargaining power, over Russia."
Later that month, Trump again harangued world leaders for doing business with Russia.
"They're funding the war against themselves. Who the hell ever heard of that one?" he said in a speech at the United Nations General Assembly. "They can't be doing what they're doing. They're buying oil and gas from Russia while they're fighting Russia."
Trump announced the diesel deal in a Truth Social post Friday afternoon after what he described as a "highly successful discussion" with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Under the agreement, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, then another 500,000 tons in November, followed by 1 million tons "immediately thereafter" and 3 million more depending on refinery conditions, Trump wrote.
The Treasury Department soon after said that Trump directed the Office of Foreign Assets Control to immediately issue a "temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market." OFAC specified that the sanctioned transactions will be authorized for about six months, until April 7.
Russia seemed to celebrate the move. "Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world," an X account associated with Putin's economic envoy Kirill Dmitriev said in response to the announcement.
But Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, whose military has started targeting Russian oil refineries, said in a searing statement that the U.S. easing sanctions on Moscow "plays into Russia's hands."
"Any easing of sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement with Russia is an obvious weakness," Zelenskyy said. "Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged."
"We count on America's fair support for our defense of life, for our defense of people in Ukraine – and on the United States having a correspondingly strong conversation with Russia," he said.
"A strong one, not a weak one," he added.
Trump thanked Putin later Friday afternoon for enabling "massive amounts of oil" to come to the U.S.
"We need oil for the world, and this is diesel, which is what we need, so we're very happy to get it," Trump told reporters before heading to Syracuse, New York.
The Trump administration has previously eased some Russian energy sanctions temporarily, though more narrowly than Friday's announcement.
Earlier this year, in an attempt to stabilize markets after the start of the Iran war, the Trump administration issued limited, 30-day waivers allowing countries to buy sanctioned Russian oil that was already in transit.
But some interpreted the latest move as a more significant step.
"It looks like Trump cut a deal with the devil," Jeremy Siegel, professor emeritus of finance at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, told CNBC's "Closing Bell" Friday afternoon.
"It's not a permanent solution at all. It's sort of a short-term Band Aid," Siegel said. "And cutting back on or eliminating sanctions on Russia for the invasion in Ukraine, I think, is a very unfortunate consequence."

Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida
October 10, 2026
Hurricane Isaias has made landfall as a Category 2 storm near Destin, Florida, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) said Friday evening.
The storm is the first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
What do we know about Hurricane Isaias?
The NHC warned of "life-threatening storm surge impacting the Gulf Coast as dangerous hurricane conditions and flash flooding spread inland."
The weather system is also bringing extreme winds, with a tornado watch issued for parts of Florida and southern Georgia.
Isaias was originally a strong Category 3 storm before making landfall. It later weakened to a Category 1 storm.
After the storm made landfall, the Florida Division of Emergency Management said the tornado watch for parts of North Florida has been extended until at least 6 a.m. local time Saturday (10 a.m. UTC).
The NHC said the hurricane has maximum sustained winds of 105 miles per hour (165 kilometers per hour).
Evacuations took place in coastal communities as the hurricane approached.
All flights at the Destin-Fort Walton Beach Airport have been canceled due to the storm. Destin is in the panhandle region of northern Florida.
Florida, Georgia and Alabama have all declared a State of Emergency due to the extreme weather system.
US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said "emergency declarations have been approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources are available to respond to #Isaias."
Florida Governor DeSantis urges residents to 'buckle down'
In a press conference, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis urged residents to "buckle down at this point. Don't be getting out on the roads."
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier also warned those "thinking about using this storm's power outages and evacuations to break in, loot, or steal: don't even try it."
"During an emergency, these crimes become first-degree felonies, punishable by up to 30 years in prison," Uthmeier said.
According to power outage tracking site PowerOutage.com, roughly 480,000 customers altogether were without electricity as of Friday evening in Florida, Georgia and Alabama.
Alabama Governor Kay Ivey said Uber, Comcast and Home Depot have offered to help Alabamians during the storm. Uber, for example, is offering free round-trip rides to state-approved evacuation shelters in Mobile and Baldwin counties.

Trump weighs livestream execution amid bipartisan backlash

US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan "absolutely" deserves the death penalty by firing squad but told reporters he has yet "to make a determination" on whether it will be livestreamed.
"I don't really care how he goes, as long as he goes," Trump said, referring to Hasan.
What did Hegseth and the Pentagon say about Hasan's execution?
Trump's remarks comes a day after the Pentagon said it would livestream the execution of 56-year-old Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist who murdered 13 people and injured 32 others in Fort Hood in Texas in 2009.
In a video shared by the Pentagon regarding the execution, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public, because people need to understand that there's serious consequence for these types of things."
Hasan is currently being held on death row in Fort Leavenworth in Kansas. His execution is slated for December 3.
He is paralyzed from the waist down and uses a wheelchair after he was shot by an officer responding to the Fort Hood shooting.
JD Vance says he would not watch livestream of execution
US Vice President JD Vance, speaking to reporters in Cincinnati on Friday, also said he doesn't know whether the livestream is "actually going to happen."
"If it is shown publicly," Vance added, "I'm not going to be watching it." Vance is a devout member of the Catholic Church, which opposes the death penalty.
"Whatever the controversy is about the method of the execution, I hope that people don't forget that this is a guy who brutally murdered a lot of innocent people," the US vice president said.
Livestream plan faces bipartisan backlash
The Pentagon's plan to broadcast the execution has been met with a fierce backlash from within Trump's own Republican Party and the opposition Democrats.
"I absolutely support the sentence of death, but livestreaming executions is what jihadists do. America is better than that," said Republican Representative Austin Scott of Georgia.
Public executions are common in Taliban-controlled Afghanistan and the so-called Islamic State (IS) also engaged in public beheadings when the group controlled large swathes of Syria and Iraq in the 2010s. Iran is another country that carries out public executions.
Republican Congressman Rob Bresnahan of Pennsylvania said "an execution shouldn't be a livestreamed spectacle."
"The focus should be on justice for the victims and their families, not turning an execution into entertainment," he said in a statement posted on X. "Their pain deserves respect, not a public show."
Democratic Congressman Eugene Vindman of Virginia, who said he oversaw legal proceedings following the Fort Hood attack, said livestreaming Hasan's execution "is what terrorists and authoritarian regimes do. It's un-American."
Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut said Pentagon chief Hegseth is "turning the Fort Hood execution into a gruesome inhumane spectacle."
The UN human rights office (OHCHR) also strongly condemned the ideaof a livestreamed execution, while the president of the United States Conference of Catholic Bishops called the plana "barbaric promotion of a culture of death."

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“This is a very unwise decision,” Pifer told Kyiv Post.
“First of all, it means that American dollars will be going to purchase Russian fuel, and that’s going to help the Russian military machine buy more missiles and bombs to use against Ukraine.”
The former ambassador argued that Trump’s decision was particularly damaging because Washington was supposed to be increasing pressure on Moscow to negotiate an end to its invasion, not offering the Kremlin economic relief.
“Second of all, it completely undercuts Trump’s own effort to mediate a solution to the Russia-Ukraine war, at a time when the US should be putting more pressure on Moscow to negotiate seriously,” Pifer said.

Little relief for US fuel prices
Pifer, now a nonresident senior fellow at the Brookings Institution and an affiliate of Stanford University’s Center for International Security and Cooperation, also challenged the economic rationale for Trump’s agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin, arguing that the initial diesel shipments were too small to significantly affect US fuel prices.
“If you look at the amount of diesel fuel that he hopes to buy – 300,000 tons in October – that amounts to less than one half a day’s consumption of diesel fuel in the United States,” he said.
“That’s not going to have that big an impact on the price of diesel.”
Trump announced Friday that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to US and global markets, followed by another 500,000 tons in November, 1 million tons afterward and an additional 3 million tons depending on the condition of Russian refineries.
The administration subsequently issued a temporary authorization allowing certain transactions involving Russian diesel, reversing restrictions intended to deprive Moscow of energy revenues.
The White House has presented the agreement as a way to ease soaring diesel prices for American farmers, truck drivers and consumers.
However, energy analysts have questioned whether the additional supplies will produce lasting price reductions, given the scale of American demand and global refining constraints.
Pifer expressed hope that the administration might reverse course.

Will Republicans challenge Trump over Graham sanctions?
The former ambassador also questioned how Republican lawmakers would respond to Trump’s decision after Congress passed legislation designed to increase economic pressure on countries purchasing Russian energy.
“It will be interesting [to see] the Republicans, who had passed the Graham sanctions bill, which was to apply greater sanctions on countries that buy Russian energy – how they’re going to react when Mr. Trump now says the United States will be buying Russian energy,” Pifer said.
Trump’s agreement came just three weeks after he signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law on Sept. 18.
The legislation was intended to expand economic pressure on Russia’s energy sector and financial networks supporting its invasion.

The talks were taking place in Florida, where US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were meeting Ukrainian and European officials to explore possible ways to end Russia’s full-scale invasion.

“I have not had much expectation that these talks would produce anything, because while Ukraine, I believe, has shown a readiness to make some painful decisions to try to find a compromise to end the war, there has been no evident movement by the Russian side,” he told Kyiv Post.
He pointed to previous statements by Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as evidence that Moscow had not softened its negotiating demands.
“The Kremlin spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said six weeks ago that Russia’s position had not changed from the one announced by Vladimir Putin in December 2024,” the former US envoy said.
“And that suggests that Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner have failed to get the Russians to move on any significant issue.”
The former ambassador said he saw little reason for optimism about the current diplomatic process.
“So I do not have many hopes for this negotiation process at this point.”
Pifer warned that Trump’s decision to ease sanctions would only reinforce Moscow’s resistance to compromise.
“This decision makes it even harder, because Moscow sees the US easing pressure rather than pushing the Kremlin to negotiate seriously,” he said.

“I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen,” Zelensky said Friday.
“And that is definitely unfair. And it is a weak decision by strong partners.”

Japanese brewer designs ‘wobbly’ beer glass to encourage responsible drinking
A craft brewery in Japan has developed a U-shaped glass that tilts unless balanced with water, promoting healthier drinking habits
The “Wobbly Beer Glass by Yona Yona Ale”, produced by Yoho Brewing based in Nagano prefecture, has been on sale since August amid growing awareness of the need for responsible drinking. The idea is that the glass, divided into two sections, will tilt if a balance between beer and water is not maintained.
Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, in guidelines released in 2024, encourages people to alternate between drinking alcoholic beverages and water to slow intoxication.
Kyoko Kitano, the employee in charge of developing the glass, was inspired by conversations with a colleague about forgetting to sip water while drinking with friends.

U.S., Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami on Oct. 9 to discuss efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine ahead of winter, on the same day Washington moved to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports.
Discussions were described by U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff as “constructive”, and covered preparations for winter, including protecting Ukraine's energy infrastructure and maintaining grain exports, as well as security guarantees and longer-term arrangements aimed at preventing future conflict. The topics of Ukraine's postwar reconstruction, economic recovery and potential accession to the European Union were also reportedly covered.
In addition to the United States, representatives from the E3 group of France, Germany and the United Kingdom, the European Commission, Ukraine and NATO took part.
Ukraine's delegation included Presidential Office head Kyrylo Budanov, Foreign Intelligence Service chief Rustem Umerov, presidential adviser Sergiy Kyslytsia and lawmaker Davyd Arakhamia, a negotiating team that has traveled to the U.S. and engaged in such discussions in the past.
Zelensky said on Oct. 8 that the negotiations were expected to last two days, Oct. 9–10, and that he anticipated a briefing from the delegation upon its return to Kyiv on Monday, Oct. 12.
In a post on X, Witkoff said that the talks helped identify areas for further consideration ahead of Washington's next engagement with Russia, but announced no concrete agreements. His statement did not indicate whether further meetings would take place on Oct. 10.
Ukrainian representatives had not publicly released their own account of the meeting at the time of publication.
The meeting coincided with U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that Russia would supply millions of tons of diesel to the United States and global markets following a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The U.S. Treasury Department subsequently issued a temporary authorization permitting purchases of Russian diesel, drawing criticism from Kyiv and European officials over the potential financial benefit to Moscow.
The Kyiv Independent reported earlier on Oct. 9 that Russia was seeking sanctions relief as part of negotiations over a possible halt to attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Moscow also wants to link a potential energy truce to ceasefire arrangements in the Black Sea.
The discussions come as Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine's energy facilities ahead of winter, threatening electricity and heating supplies across the country.

Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida with severe effects expected across several states
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-10
01:44:33 UTC
10:44:33 KST

Hurricane Isaias crashed into the US Gulf coast on Friday as a dangerous category 2 storm, hammering communities in Alabama and the Florida panhandle with damaging winds, heavy rain, flooding and life-threatening storm surges.
The first hurricane of the Atlantic season made landfall near Destin, Florida, the National Hurricane Center said. It had maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (169 kph). The storm weakened to just below major hurricane status before it came ashore.
“The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads,” Florida’s governor, Ron DeSantis, said at a news conference, adding flash flooding would be a hazard “throughout the region”.
In Pensacola, about 50 miles (80km) west of Destin an Agence France-Presse reporter witnessed howling winds rip the roofs from some homes and businesses, snapping tree branches as the power went out.
“Things are flying really fast, and I’ve never seen wind this fast before, so it’s intense, it’s scary,” Jonathan Ramos, a 40-year-old government employee, said from his hotel in Pensacola, where the power went out.
“I don’t recommend people coming down here for fun to do this.”
President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House late Friday night: “We’re watching it very closely, the hurricane,” adding that it was “under control”.
Forecasters had expected Isaias to weaken from its peak earlier on Friday as a major category 3 hurricane because of shifts in wind speed.
But even as a weaker storm system, the NHC warned of a life-threatening storm surge affecting the Gulf Coast as dangerous hurricane conditions and flash floods spread inland. The hurricane is expected to cross Alabama and into the Tennessee Valley on the weekend, the agency added.
Warnings included a storm surge of up to 7ft (2.1 meters) along the Alabama-Florida line, and powerful wind gusts reaching parts of northern Georgia.
In the Florida Panhandle, Isaias’s early impacts also came into view. In Panama city beach, Noaa officials observed a water level 5.4 feet (1.64 meters) above average. About 125 miles west, at the Pensacola city hall, a wind gust up to 102 mph (164km/h) was recorded.
Powerful gusts of wind and heavy rainfall appeared to down the canopy of a Crestview gas station on Friday evening, according to a video captured by meteorologist Nick Stewart. The tattered cover hung on top of a filling station.
“The storm is here. Buckle down at this point. Don’t be getting out on the roads,” Florida governor Ron DeSantis said at a news conference, adding that flash flooding would be a hazard “throughout the region”.
The governors of Mississippi, Alabama and Florida all declared states of emergency ahead of the storm’s arrival, urging some residents of coastal communities to evacuate and many more to prepare for the storm’s likely violent arrival.
Alabama governor Kay Ivey announced shortly before the hurricane made landfall that Donald Trump had approved the emergency declaration for her state. “This will help cut tape for our federal partners to aid in any response,” Ivey said.
The Mobile office of the National Weather Service warned parts of Florida could see “extremely dangerous” tornado-like winds.
By Friday evening, nearly 500,000 customers had lost power across Alabama and Florida, according to PowerOutage.com.
“Things are going to get really, really treacherous,” Jamie Rhome, deputy director for the National Hurricane Center, told the AP.
Florida’s national guard deployed roughly 5,000 soldiers and airmen to aid with the response, the AP reported. Some prisons were also evacuating their incarcerated populations. Most flights were grounded at several airports in Florida’s Panhandle.
The state guard has deployed about 400 soldiers to assess the hurricane’s damage and assist with route clearance, among other duties.
The Florida fish and wildlife conservation commission has readied 10 airboats, 18 shallow-draft boats, nine ATVs and six larger platform vessels in the event of damage or flooding.
Uber has also partnered with the state to offer free-round trips, up to $40 each way, to and from state-approved evacuation shelters.
Isaias is notable as one of the two latest-forming Atlantic hurricanes on record, tying a record set on 8 October 1905. None of the eight previous named storms of the 2026 Atlantic season intensified above tropical storm status.
Ahead of the storm, oil and gas producers shut down a significant share of offshore production in the Gulf, which accounts for almost 15% of crude pumped annually in the US.
In a sign of how serious the warnings are, dozens of Waffle Houses in the Florida Panhandle were closed, according to the company’s website. The beloved Southern breakfast chain is known for staying open through severe weather and often is a measuring stick of a storm’s severity.
Kelsei Frazier, a Florida native living in Pace who is no stranger to hurricanes, knows all about the Waffle House Index.
“We joke because if Waffle House is still open, then you know it’s not a bad hurricane, but all the Waffle Houses that I know of within at least a normal range from us are closed,” said Frazier. “Which is a pretty big deal.”
Associated Press contributed reporting.

Trump renews bid to fire Fed’s Cook with fresh White House inquiry
- Trump has opened a fresh White House inquiry into Fed Governor Lisa Cook, accusing her of false mortgage statements and seeking a possible firing before congressional elections.
- Cook’s lawyers say there is no legal basis to remove her, and they plan to show she did not commit mortgage fraud at the Nov 5 closed hearing.
- The move renews fears over Fed independence after a Supreme Court ruling set a “cause” process for removal, while critics call Trump’s action a “kangaroo court”.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – United States President Donald Trump launched a new inquiry into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook weeks before congressional elections, convening an investigative committee and ordering an unprecedented White House hearing into allegations she made false statements on mortgage applications.
Trump has been trying to fire Cook for more than a year, as he moves to exert more control over a central bank he says is refusing for political reasons to lower interest rates. Lawyers for Cook said on Oct 9 any fair hearing would show there is no legal basis for firing her.
“As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law,” Trump said in a notice on the White House website on Oct 9.
“To assist me in carrying out that responsibility, the committee shall investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is ‘cause’ for Governor Cook’s removal,” according to the notice dated Oct 7.
The committee will hold a closed, in-person four-hour hearing at the White House on Nov 5 “to consider the evidence and allegations against Governor Cook”, the presidential memorandum said.
The hearing falls two days after elections that will determine if Trump’s Republican Party maintains control of the US House and Senate, whose members are charged with confirming presidential nominees to the Fed.
A successful removal of Cook would create a vacancy on the Fed’s seven-member Board.
If the hearing is “anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board”, Cook’s lawyers Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen said in a statement.
“Governor Cook welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her.”
They said they had engaged with the White House about the process.
Trump first tried to fire Cook, the first black woman to serve on the central bank’s board, in August 2025.
No US president has ever tried to fire a sitting Fed governor before. Central banks are widely seen as needing political independence to ensure their ability to fight inflation as needed.
Supreme court ruling on Fed removal
Cook sued, saying she had done nothing wrong. The case led to the US Supreme Court ruling earlier in 2026 that the president could not remove a Fed governor at will, and needed to follow a clear process laying out a “cause” for firing and allowing for a defence.
The ruling left Cook in her position, but kicked the case against her back to a federal district court, where Judge Jia Cobb in September set a Nov 6 deadline for the lawyers of Trump and Cook to submit a joint proposal for the proceedings.
Cook was appointed to the Fed board in 2022 by former US President Joe Biden, a Democrat, and was re-appointed in 2023 to a term that lasts until 2038.
She has always cast her vote with the majority on the Fed’s policy-making committee, which in September raised interest rates under the leadership of Kevin Warsh, whom Trump appointed to succeed Jerome Powell in May.
“Trump appears to believe that the reason the Fed has turned hawkish is because his chosen chairman Warsh is boxed in by a hawkish and politically hostile Fed board,” Evercore ISI analyst Krishna Guha wrote.
Trump’s creation of the inquiry committee “constitutes a re-upping of his threat to Fed independence and will be counter-productive in terms of the President’s desire for lower interest rates”.
Trump’s chief economic policy adviser Kevin Hassett, Equal Employment Opportunity Commission chair Andrea Lucas and acting Office of Government Ethics director Keith Sonderling will comprise the newly formed committee, the memorandum said.
Those members, their representatives or Department of Justice personnel will question Cook for “no longer than four hours”.
The committee will make its recommendation to Trump on whether he has cause to remove Cook “as soon as practicable” after a Nov 10 deadline for Cook to submit any post-hearing statement, the memo said.
Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee that oversees the Fed, called the hearing a “kangaroo court” and part of Trump’s “dangerous quest to illegally take over our nation’s central bank”.
Trump has contended that Powell, who has remained at the Fed as governor, may have engaged in financial misconduct related to the Fed’s building renovations. The allegation sparked a now-closed Department of Justice criminal investigation and was rejected in September by an independent watchdog agency. REUTERS

CAIRO, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China defeated Thailand 2-0 in the semifinals of the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Junior Team Championships in Cairo on Friday evening, setting up a title clash with Malaysia on Saturday.
The Chinese team overcame an early deficit to secure victory at the Cairo Stadium Indoor Halls Complex, winning two straight sets under the tournament's relay scoring format, in which players compete across five disciplines and accumulate points for their teams.
Yin Yiqing, an 18-year-old Chinese player, said the match was challenging because China was trailing when she entered the court. "We had prepared thoroughly for the team competition format and practiced it many times during training," she told Xinhua after the match.

Looking ahead to Saturday's final, Luo said, "If I get the chance to play, I will give it my all and fight for every point. I hope Team China can achieve a great result in the end."

US Justice Department scrutinises Binance compliance with 2023 settlement deal

- Binance agreed to a US$4.3 billion penalty in 2023 and must report misconduct. If it breached the deal, it could face revived charges and more fines.
- DOJ official Tysen Duva urged crypto firms to self-report fraud and praised public-private cooperation. Binance said it is improving controls and will keep working with law enforcement.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) is scrutinising whether Binance Holdings breached a landmark settlement with the US government, as the authorities probe activity on the platform for potential Iran sanctions violations.
Tysen Duva, head of DOJ’s criminal division, said in an interview this week that officials were reviewing Binance’s compliance with its 2023 agreement.
Duva declined to discuss specifics and did not say that Binance was in violation of the settlement, under which the company agreed to a US$4.3 billion (S$5.5 billion) penalty, pleaded guilty to violating banking rules and accepted increased compliance controls.
In September, the US Attorney’s Office in Manhattan, which is leading the probe and working with the criminal division in Washington, sought forfeiture of US$61 million that it said was generated from Iranian black-market oil sales and laundered through Binance.
Federal prosecutors have been investigating whether the operator of the world’s biggest crypto exchange committed violations of US sanctions on Iran by not stopping certain trading on its platform, Bloomberg has reported.
“There is an ongoing investigation there that we are involved with,” Duva said in the interview. “But beyond that, we’re not going to get into specifics about exactly what the status of the facts are, how it’s developing.”
The DOJ said it does not comment on ongoing investigations in response to follow-up questions.
Neither the company nor its employees have been accused of wrongdoing and probes can end without charges or lawsuits being filed.
“We are continually working to enhance our controls, and we are fully committed to cooperating with law enforcement,” Binance said in a statement.
Self-reporting
Duva also praised Binance and other digital asset companies for helping the US thwart cyber scams and frauds, especially those committed by transnational criminal organisations.
He has been encouraging companies to come forward and self-report, favouring settlements over what could become costly prosecutions.
“I want to focus really on the positive part of the relationship that we’re trying to build with the crypto companies and tech companies,” Duva said.
“The early returns have been great with social media, with crypto exchanges, and we’re very excited to really press that and continue this. A big part of this is these public-private partnerships.”
More broadly, DOJ is urging companies to self-report possible fraud, favouring settlements with companies that proactively disclose potential violations over what could become costly and time-consuming prosecutions, Duva said.
Binance is required under the 2023 settlement to report to the government any evidence or allegations of misconduct related to federal laws governing money laundering, banking transactions and sanctions violations.
If Binance is found to have breached the deal, the company could be subject to prosecution for the criminal activity that was resolved under the settlement, potentially facing revived charges and billions of dollars in additional fines.
Since the 2023 settlement, Binance has sought to emphasise its cooperation with law enforcement and regulators. The company said in a blog post in February that overall, more than 1,500 people, or about 25% of its global headcount, worked on compliance.
Binance’s former chief executive Zhao Changpeng pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering programme and ended up serving four months in prison.
Zhao, also known by his initials, CZ, was pardoned by US President Donald Trump in October and has been travelling the world promoting adoption of cryptocurrency in places ranging from Dubai to Pakistan. Bloomberg

Renoir paintings worth $10.5 million missing after museum heist
Two paintings by the French Impressionist artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir that were stolen from a museum in southern France a month ago have been recovered, the town’s mayor said.
“These two paintings are not simply works of art. They are part of our city’s history,” Bryan Masson, the mayor of Cagnes-sur-Mer, near Nice, said on Friday. “Knowing they have been recovered is an immense relief.”
Six people have been arrested in connection with the theft, local authorities said. Masson did not say where the paintings were found or in what condition.
How the theft unfolded
Two thieves broke into the Renoir Museum a little before 6am on September 8, cutting through a fence to enter the grounds, smashing a window and using an electric saw to cut the clips securing the frames, Masson said at the time.
He described them as “well equipped” and “well informed”.
The museum alarm sounded at 5:48am, and municipal police arrived five minutes later, forcing the thieves to flee.
They had taken four paintings, valued by the mayor at about nine million euros ($10.5m).
Two of the stolen works – Renoir’s “Portrait of Madame Pichon” and “Coco Reading” – were later found dropped in the museum garden, the prosecutor’s office said at the time.
The two works that remained missing were “Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano” and “Young Woman at the Well”, the office said.
Police said last month that the thieves were not first-time offenders and had scoped out the premises.
The Marseille prosecutor opened a theft investigation into an organised gang, and the national office for trafficking in cultural goods joined the probe.
A string of museum heists
The museum, opened in 1960, is in the painter’s last home, where he died in 1919.
“This incident should serve as a warning about the protection of our museums,” Masson said after the robbery.
The theft came less than a year after jewels worth about $100m were stolen from the Louvre in Paris in a daylight robbery.
The four suspected robbers have been arrested, but the jewels have not been found.
In August, Italian police said they had recovered paintings by Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse worth more than $10.4m that were stolen from a museum in March.
